An unconformity above the Little Dal Group presumably divides this Precambrian succession into Helikian and Hadrynian age sequences. All of these units to at least as high as the "grainstone subunit" of the Little Dal Group are cut by diabase intrusions, which are thought to be lithologically equivalent to the diabase sills sampled for the present study within the Tsezotene Formation (Aitken and Cook 1974). SYMONS Department of Geology, Universiry of Windsor, Windsor, Ont., Canada N9B 3P4 Received March 16, 1981 Revision accepted December 4, 1981 Early Aphebian Gowganda sedimentary rocks and intruding Nipissing diabase sills were sampled for paleomagnetic study at 88 sites (-500 cores, -1000 specimens) along two -42km long profiles extending north from the Grenville Front into the Cobalt Plate of the Southern Structural Province in the River Valley - Lake Temagami area of Ontario. After AF demagnetization a postfolding pre-Nipissing -2200 Ma remanence was found in eight of the 37 Gowganda sediment sites that were >2 km north of the front, giving a pole at 109W, 63"N (4 = lo0, dm = 19"). The Nippissing diabase from >2 km north of the front retains a stable antiparallel prefolding N1 remanence direction in 22 of 40 sites, giving apole position of 85W, 17"s (d, = 6", d,,, = 10"). These "south and down" remanence directions found in the southern portion of the plate contrast with the antiparallel "north and up" directions found in the northern portion, thereby indicating the occurrence of either two nearly cogenetic Nipissing intrusive even

three "Nipissing" sites give a pole at 164"W, 3"N, which is close to the known pole for the later -1.25 Ga Sudbtuy olivine diabase dikes. One site is adjacent to a large dike and two were found on thin-section examination to be olivine diabase. The eight sites in Gowganda sediment matrix and conglomerate clasts and in Nipissing diabase from within <2 km from the front were found to have a postfolding metamorphic remanence with a Grenville orogenic pole at 45 W, 5 1% (4 = 19", dm = 21"). Finally, the results lead to a suggested revision in the APW path for the -2300--1650 Ma interval for North America. The Gowganda Formation comprises polymictic conglomerate, quartz arenite, arkose, and argillite and has a maximum thickness of 1500m (Roscoe 1973). It gives a concordant early Aphebian Rb-Sr whole-rock isochron age of 2290 + 90 Ma (Fairbairn et al. 1969). Some of these irregutar sills are hundreds of metres thick (Dressler 1979). In this work the Grenville episode is detected by limited isotopic exchange between adjacent minerals. The sampled anorthosite plutons occur either closely associated with monzonitic to granitic rocks or as small lenses in rnigmatitic gneisses (Ontario Department of Mines 1974). These gneissic, interlayered (rarely mas- sive) anorthosites have the same gneissosity as the associated monzonitic to granitic rocks and the migma- titic gneisses, which suggests a common deformation and metamorphic history. An additional complexity in analyzing the remanence components is the possibility that metamorphic chemi- cal alteration during any episode may well produce hematite with a highly stable chemical remanent mag- netization (CRM) component. In this study, three methods of statistical analysis are used and compared. These are conventional two-tiered screening, specimen level screening, and population level screening. Conventional two-tiered statistical analysis uses the two specimen directions as a measure of the core remanence homogeneity. The upper member of the Peel Sound Formation has been interpreted as deltaic alluvial fan and piedmont deposits with paleocurrent directions towards the west. Miall (1970) distinguished several facies belts, which are, from east to west: (1) conglom- erate facies; (2) conglomerate-sandstone facies: inter- bedded conglomerate, fine to coarse red sandstone and red siltstone, deposited by low sinuosity braided streams; (3) sandstone facies: point bar deposition in high sinuosity streams; (4) sandstone-carbonate facies: red, pink, and buff sandstones, interbedded with dolo- mites deposited in an estuarine environment. Miall (1970) gave a fifth facies, the carbonate facies, but this is now considered to belong to the Drake Bay Formation (Thorsteinsson 1980). Paleomagnetic samples were collected from facies zones 2, 3, and 4. Age The upper member of the Peel Sound Formation is of Early Devonian (late Lochkovian) age (Thorsteinsson 1980). The magnetic directions from which the poles are calculated are derived from vector analysis of thermal, chemical, and alternating magnetic field demagnetization results. Normal and reversed polarities are recorded for the northerly pole, whereas the pole at the equator reveals mainly a normal polarity. The magnetite- and hematite-residing LD-A direction is a pre-folding magnetization (pre-Late Cretaceous) which has a mean direction of D = 265", I = -26" (ag5 = 4"). A second magnetization, LD-B, thought to be residing in the red hematite pigment, has a similar mean direction at D = 273", I = -09" (ag5 = 10"). Park (1981~) considered that both these magnetizations were acquired "soon after rock genesis." A third direction, LD-C, (D = 289", I = +79", ag5 = 7"), which characteristically has low blocking temperatures, was suggested to be a "goethite" weathering component of Cretaceous age. The lavas have a much more complicated remanence history. There seems to be little obvious correlation between the remanence directions from the two sections at which the lavas were sampled. At the Keele River area, three well defined groups of remanence directions could be separated. Because of its occurrence in the unaltered lava, and as an univectorial magnetization that resides in both magnetite and hematite, the direction LD-L is considered to provide the best estimate of the magnetic field direction during lava extrusion for the Keele River area. The reference technique was the least-squares fitting of lines to segments of demagnetization trajectory (Kirschvink 1980). Minimum acceptance criteria adopted for this technique were: a minimum of four points on a line, with a maximum angular deviation of 7.5". Other techniques included least-squares fits to great-circle distributions (Halls 1976), and sequential vector subtractions. For these techniques, which only provided supporting evidence, the minimum acceptance criteria were, respectively: a minimum of four great-circle segments with arc lengths greater than 25", required to define an overprint component; and a maximum angular difference of 10" (determined by vector subtraction) between three sequentially subtracted vectors from the same specimen, the accepted direction being a vector mean of the three components. Site mean directions representative of the individual remanence components present at each site were calculated using the standard Fisher (1953) statistical techniques or the Kirschvink- derived (1980) specimen data directions. directional_or_weak_substitution_warning.excerpt: The Little Dal lavas were sampled at two localities separated by approximately 150 krn. From two sections through the lava sequence near the Keele River area (63"48'N, 231°30'E) 10 sites were obtained for paleomagnetic analysis. Six sites were sampled at a second locality near Coates Lake in the Thundercloud Range (62"24'N, 233"4OtE). At each site at least six 2 in. (5 cm) cores were collected by field drilling. Two specimens were sliced from each core. The bedding orientation at each sampling locality was measured on the nearest sedimentary unit. The difference in structural orientation between the two areas provided a possible fold test of remanence age. At the Keele River sites the beds dip moderately to the west, and at the Coates Lake sites the beds dip steeply to the east. As this folding was probably developed during the Mesozoic orogeny, the fold test does not provide a precise age control of the magnetization; magnetizations passing a positive fold test are merely constrained to the interval Late Precambrian through Cretaceous.
